title: ENDEX: Thursday Evening, Riverside Closed, Shelter to Red Cross

fields.resolution: ENDEX. ENDEX. ENDEX. The exercise clock reads 09:30 EDT, and the SimCell has run the recovery afternoon out to Thursday evening, 20:30, March 25, 2027: Sugar Camp Run is below flood stage at the Mill Street gauge and falling, and the second rain band has passed north. Riverside Hall stays closed until the Marlowe building inspector gives written clearance after tomorrow's 09:00 walk-through, Kessler Fieldhouse and the Student Union ballroom are being handed to the Red Cross chapter with a reconciled count, and the damage figures and displaced population count have gone to the Ohio Emergency Management Agency. This concludes the exercise; stop play now.
finalState: Mill Street gauge below 7.0 ft flood stage and falling; Dairy Lane crossing reopens only after Facilities inspects it
Riverside Hall closed tonight and tomorrow night pending the building inspector's written clearance
Kessler Fieldhouse and the Student Union ballroom are being handed to the Red Cross chapter with the registration log, a reconciled daily count and the FNSS supports in place
Preliminary damage figures and the displaced population count have been sent to the Ohio Emergency Management Agency
Every seat's notification log, shelter log and decision log stays on its table as evidence
fields.hotWashTransition: Thank you, everyone. Hang up the SimCell phones, put the markers down and leave your notification log, shelter log and decision log on the table. We are not taking a break. We move straight into the hot wash here in Hargrove Hall 120, and the no-fault rule we read at 14:00 still applies. Student Evaluators, you open with the timeline you recorded.
fields.hotWashMethod: Evaluator timeline first, then each seat in turn answers three questions: what happened, what did the plan say, what would you change.
hotWashQuestions: The 0720 AM forecast put the crest at 10.8 ft near 10:30. When was the Riverside order given, what did the decision log name as its basis, and how much of the 90-minute sweep time did the order leave?
How long after the 07:50 roof-rescue post did the first MSU Alert and the correction go out, and was the message the same on every channel, including the parent line?
Riverside's roster was 680. Where did the count stand at handover: registered, signed out, confirmed off campus, still unconfirmed, and the 3 walk-ins who were not on the roster?
What confirmation passed between the seats before the Riverside main breaker was opened, and who confirmed that the elevators and floors 9 to 11 were clear?
Which Lot C, library and diesel decisions were made against a stage trigger or a clearance time, and which were made only after the water got there?
fields.facilitatorNote: Collect every seat's logs and the evaluator forms before the hot wash starts. Hold the hot wash to 16:20 to 16:35 so the reflection prompts and sheet collection finish by 16:50. Make sure each quote goes to the student who was speaking for the seat during that rotation.
fields.scenarioTitle: Ninety Minutes: Flash Flood, Evacuation & Campus Shelter

instructorNote: This card stops play and opens the evaluator-led hot wash. Check that every seat hands in its logs, and that the Student Evaluators present their recorded times for the Level changes, the Riverside order, the first MSU Alert, the roof-rumor correction and the count reconciliation. They should score each seat against the role rubrics on a no-fault basis.
